Let me read this script cold, as a 15-18 year old student who didn't choose this book, reading it the night before it's due. I need to report my honest reactions, issue by issue, page by page.

Let me actually read through this as a cold reader would.

**Issue 01 — Keel**

Page 1: Full-page splash. Mountain basin, three cities stacked: Keel below, Halyard midway, Oasis above. Alex Phantum, 17, fixing a pump with a salvaged bracket that doesn't match the approved diagram. Captions: "2043." "OASIS. HALYARD. KEEL." SFX: THRUMM.

Okay, this is a strong opening image actually. The three-tier city is instantly readable — poor at the bottom, rich at the top. I've seen this before (Metropolis, Elysium, every YA dystopia) but it's clear. The name "Alex Phantum" — Phantum? Like phantom? That's a bit on the nose. The kid's name is basically "Ghost." Hmm.

Page 2: The supervisor exchange — "That isn't the approved repair." / "Then don't approve it." / "Just notice it works." That's a decent line, establishes Alex. Then the checkpoint screen: DEBT TRANSFER DAY, age verified seventeen, parental household liability transfer complete, guarantor Adrian Phantum whereabouts unrecorded, debt balance 418,607 credits, earned today 40 credits, projected clearance 28.7 years, travel status restricted. "Happy birthday, Phantum."

Okay — this is efficient. I get it immediately: on your 17th birthday you inherit your parents' debt. That's brutal and clear. The math: 418,607 credits at 40/day = 28.7 years. Checks out roughly (418,607/40 = 10,465 days ≈ 28.7 years). Fine. The guard's "Happy birthday" lands. This page pulled me in.

Wait — "TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED" — okay so he can't leave. And then panel 4: "One day, I'm leaving." Good setup.

Page 3: Ada Veyra shows up with tea. Banter: "You look expensive." / "It came with a twenty-eight-year warranty." Good line. "You say that like you invented debt." / "I only inherited it." Also good. Then Ada: "Then don't spend them proving he was right about people leaving." Hmm, that's a bit of a riddle-line. Let me parse: Alex's dad left (or is gone, whereabouts unrecorded), and people apparently say he ran off — gambling debts? Ada says don't leave just to prove the story that people leave. Actually wait, re-reading: "don't spend them proving he was right about people leaving" — meaning if Alex leaves, he confirms the pattern? I had to read that twice. And "I think everybody's been very sure of a story nobody can show you. What if they're wrong?" — pointing at the sealed mine. So the dad's story is murky. Okay, intrigued.

Page 4: The photograph with Adrian's face folded out of view — that's a nice touch, withholding the face. Grandmother calls Alex "Adrian" — dementia. "The worst part isn't that she forgets. It's the stories she makes up about him. That he was working. Not gambling." Okay so the official story: dad was a gambler who ran off. Grandma says he was working. "They're all pointing at a door nobody opens." The sealed mine. Fine, clear enough mystery.

Page 5: Grandmother scene. "He's closer than you think." — ominous. The hand-bound book with a water-drop mark. "Your father never liked seeing it left out."

Page 6: Book goes into the gap, CLICK, bookshelf swings open, secret workshop. "He said you'd know when you were ready." / "When did he say that?" / "Before he went to work." Okay — so dad hid a workshop behind the bookshelf and grandma knew all along. This is a big swing. A secret room behind the bookshelf in a cramped Keel apartment? I mean, it's a genre move. Fine, I'll go with it. But wait — grandma has dementia and calls him Adrian half the time, but she's been keeping this secret perfectly for fifteen years? That's... convenient. Actually the script kind of acknowledges she's lucid in moments. Hmm. As a reader I might notice: the apartment is tiny and crowded (page 5 says repaired furniture, plants in reused containers) but there's a whole hidden workshop? Where does it physically fit? Whatever, genre.

Page 7: Workshop frozen in dust. The chalkboard has the same looping equation as Alex's casino chip. A child-sized figure under a dust sheet. A key with the water-drop.

Wait — the casino chip. Alex has been carrying a casino chip etched with a looping equation since page 2. Where did he get it? It's never said. It's presented as this meaningful object — "casino chip" implies the gambling story — but the equation matches dad's chalkboard. So the chip is dad's? Presumably. But nobody says "this was my father's chip" or "I found this." As a reader I notice the chip keeps appearing and I don't know its origin. Ledger item: casino chip — page 2, never explained where Alex got it. Actually it might be implied it's the one thing he has of his father's. But it's not stated.

Page 8: Bi11bot revealed. Child-sized robot, brass, titanium, ceramic ivory, old scarf. Key, CLICK, eyes ignite. "...Well. That took longer than expected." Good robot line.

"Bi11bot" — spelled with two 1's. B-i-1-1-b-o-t. On the page as a reader, I'd read "Billbot"? "Bi-eleven-bot"? Tomas later calls him "B1." So it's B-1-1? The name is a bit awkward to read. Minor.

Page 9: "You're taller than your father predicted." "Everyone in Keel claims they knew my father." "I'm not everyone. I was in the room." Good. The bet about the chip: "Your father bet me you'd throw it in a river. I said you wouldn't." "...I thought about it." "Thinking about it isn't doing it." Nice exchange. "Now, shall we say hello to your father?"

Page 10: Adrian's hologram. "You deserve answers. But they have to be earned. Trust Bi11bot. Question everything. Especially me." Grandma: "I heard that." — good beat. The photo unfolded, matching face. Okay, the face reveal pays off the folded photo. Nice.

Hmm wait — "answers have to be earned" — this is the dead dad making his son do chores for answers. As a reader I might find that mildly annoying but it's genre-standard.

Page 11: Three tools: the Measure (brass), the Maker's Seal (bronze open hand), three Covenant bands (dark). "Tools for three different kinds of damage." The maintenance record example: worker's repair credited to facility, worker carried injury and wage penalty. "Paper-clean." Then: "So none of them fixes the damage." "Correct. They make it harder to hide who saw it, who made it, and who owes a response."

Okay, this is where the book starts getting... expository. The Measure measures physical truth, the Seal records who did the work, the Covenant bands are about promises. I sort of get it. But "three different kinds of damage" / "That depends who gets hurt" is vague. And the names — Measure, Maker's Seal, Covenant — these are capital-T Things now. Ledger: the Measure, Maker's Seal, Covenant bands — introduced page 11, explained only abstractly. The Covenant bands especially: "No reciprocal promise has been made" — okay so they're promise-detectors? Promise-recorders? Unclear.

Page 12: Alex presses the amber node, pulse goes up the spine, Oasis control room: "LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED / SOURCE: KEEL SECTOR." Mera Vale chooses TRACK over REPORT TO ALPHA. Then Bi11bot's map: "The first node is under the pit." "And the second?" "Higher. Unconfirmed."

Wait — what node? First node of what? The script jumps from "here are three tools" to "the first node is under the pit." Node of what system? The water system? The Covenant? Alpha? I'm confused here. Also: who is Mera Vale? She just appears in a control room choosing TRACK. No introduction. Ledger: Mera Vale — page 12, appears with no explanation. Alpha — mentioned page 12 ("REPORT TO ALPHA"), never explained what Alpha is. It's clearly some AI/system authority but the book never says. Ledger: Alpha — page 12, used as if known, never defined. Actually wait, page 7 said "pre-Alpha pipes" — so Alpha was mentioned on page 7 first. "Pre-Alpha pipes" implies Alpha is an era-defining thing. But never explained.

Also why does Alex press the node? What is he trying to do? He just... sends a pulse up the spine. Why? Because Bi11bot told him to? The motivation is thin. And Mera choosing TRACK sets up a threat, fine.

Page 13: Morning. Ada enters with a paper map. "You said you were leaving." "The city disagreed." Shift reassigned to Site 6. "The official map skips these." Ink ticks every third junction. "Look for what doesn't belong." Medicine first — Alex slides medicine to grandma. "One shift. Then we're gone." "Not gone. Looking."

Wait — where did Ada get this altered map with ink ticks? She just has it. And how does she know about the junctions? She's been in on this since when? Last we saw, Alex found the workshop — did he tell Ada off-panel? Page 11 had Ada already in the workshop ("Alex and Ada stand opposite him"). So between page 10 and 11, Ada got brought in. Fine, but the map with ticks — who made it? "Ada spreads the altered map" — altered by whom? Ledger-ish. Actually maybe it's meant to be Ada's own annotations. Unclear.

Page 14: Site 6. Foreman-7 — "a large human man" with a node at his throat. Why is he called Foreman-7 if he's human? Is the -7 a designation? Weird name for a human. Tomas introduced. Cable snaps, frame drops on Tomas, Alex crosses the yellow line, wage forfeited −40 CR. "Forty credits." "I know." — a full day's wage, callback to page 2. Good.

Page 15: Alex frees Tomas. "That's not regulation." "It works." "...So it does." Tomas recognizes Bi11bot: "B1." "I knew your father." Water-drop carved in wrist guard. "Adrian asked me to keep a door for whoever came with B1." "Why me?" "You stopped for a stranger." Key. "Go stand by the bulkhead. Look bored."

Okay so Adrian set up a whole network of people fifteen years ago waiting for his son. Tomas has oiled the lock for fifteen years. That's a long con. Fine, genre.

Page 16: Tomas slams emergency lever, mist, "Wrong button! My fault!" — Tomas sacrifices himself? "Someone has to make this look like an accident." What happens to Tomas after? Never shown. He walks into the mist blocking Foreman-7. Does he get punished? Disappeared? The book never comes back to it — well, page 54 shows Tomas near the board with Foreman-7, both "ordinary participants," so apparently fine. But at the time, as a reader, I'd wonder.

"It’s sweating." "Abandoned mines don’t." — good line, creepy. The mine isn't abandoned/dead — something's active. 

Page 17: Old works. Alpha's cached survey says straight; Ada's map says left. Clean oiled bolts say left. Drone: "Remain for protective detention." "Protective?" "A versatile word." Good.

Panel 3: "Alex, Ada, Bi11bot, and TJ are not yet together" — wait, TJ? Who is TJ? Panel 4: "Bi11bot's chest opens and releases magnetic brass, titanium, and ceramic parts. TJ assembles into a small dog-shaped robot." Oh — TJ is a dog-robot that assembles from parts in Bi11bot's chest. Okay, that's a surprise but readable. TJ = the dog bot. But the panel 3 description literally says "Alex, Ada, Bi11bot, and TJ are not yet together" before TJ exists as assembled — that's a script note that would confuse... well, as a reader of the comic I'd just see the parts come out and assemble. Fine. But also — wait, where did Ada go? Page 16 Alex went through the bulkhead... alone? Page 17 panel 3 shows Ada crawling through a separate storm culvert. When did they split up? Page 16 shows Alex reaching the bulkhead with Bi11bot in the bag — Ada isn't mentioned. Did Ada come to Site 6? Page 13 said "One shift. Then we're gone." Page 14 shows Alex at Site 6 — Ada not mentioned. So Ada just appears in the old works via a separate entrance. I had to flip back: when did Ada enter the mine? Confusing. Actually page 17 panel 3 says "Ada crawls through a separate storm culvert entrance with her paper map" — so she went in separately, but the script never showed her deciding to. As a reader: "Wait, Ada's here? Since when?"

Page 18: Hidden water chamber. KEEL RESIDENTIAL pipe nearly dry, UPLINK INDUSTRIAL trembling with flow. Gauge 62%. Measure clamps: "REPORTED TO KEEL: 62% / DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%." "That's not a mistake." "No. It's a maintained choice." TRACE vs VERIFY choice: private exit or public broadcast. "If I send it, we lose the quiet route." "Then send it where people can see." VERIFY pressed. Cliffhanger: workers crowd screens showing 62/18. Mera's authorization reaches a conduit valve: "CONDUIT SEGMENT — RELEASE AUTHORIZED." Water fills behind them as they climb into the conduit. HISS—THOOM.

Wait — Mera authorized the release? The same Mera who chose TRACK? So Mera is flooding the conduit to kill them? Or is this Alpha? The screen says "Mera's authorization reaches a conduit valve" — so Mera is trying to drown them?? That's a heel turn with zero setup. Or is it meant to be ambiguous — like Alpha did it and Mera's tracking enabled it? The panel says "Mera's authorization reaches a conduit valve. SCREEN: CONDUIT SEGMENT — RELEASE AUTHORIZED." Reads like Mera did it. Hmm. But in Issue 3 Mera is a sympathetic character who suppressed Ada's risk reports. So the flood... was it Mera trying to kill them? This is never really addressed later! Let me check... Issue 3, Mera helps them, explains the past. The flood authorization is never mentioned again as far as I can see. That's a dangling thread. As a reader: "Wait, the Oasis lady tried to drown them? And then in issue 3 she's on their side? What?"

Actually, hold on. Maybe the intent is that Alpha authorized it and Mera couldn't stop it, or Mera's TRACK action triggered Alpha. But the page as written says "Mera's authorization reaches a conduit valve." Cold read: Mera tried to kill them. Then Issue 3 never reckons with that. Finding.

Also the 62/18 broadcast: "If I send it, we lose the quiet route" — why? Sending data doesn't physically block the exit... oh, I guess VERIFY reveals their location, so drones come. Okay, that tracks. And the cliffhanger is decent: water flooding in. Real cliffhanger? They're climbing into a "near-empty conduit" as water fills behind them — danger, yes, but I don't deeply fear for them. It's issue 1 of 3, they're not dying. Moderate pull.

Issue 1 verdict: pulled in by pages 1-2, the debt transfer. Slowed at page 11's tool exposition. Confused by "first node," Mera, Ada's sudden presence in the mine. Last page: I'd read issue 2, yes.

**Issue 02 — Halyard**

Page 19: Storm drain bursts, they crawl out soaked. "Still disagreeable." "Halyard may consider that a distinction." TJ's rear leg clicks a beat late — cute detail.

Wait — they climbed into a near-empty conduit as water filled behind them, and now they just... crawl out of a storm drain in Halyard. The flood resolved off-panel. Fine, standard issue-break cheat, but as a reader I notice: the cliffhanger danger just evaporated. Also — weren't they wanted? The drone said "remain for protective detention." They broadcast the 62/18 data. And now they walk around Halyard? Alex has a travel restriction! He was RESTRICTED — how is he in Halyard? Nobody stops him? Page 21 he presents his identity band at a public registry and nothing happens about the travel restriction. Hmm. Actually maybe the broadcast made them... no. Ledger: travel restriction — page 2, then ignored when Alex travels to Halyard and later Oasis (page 37 has a temporary pass for Oasis, so Oasis is addressed, but Halyard?).

Page 20: Halyard. Contribution kiosk: worker's component accepted, ownership: HOUSE HELION, creator bonus 14 credits. "She made it." "The House owns it." "Keel restricts bodies. Halyard is more ambitious." "It restricts what people make." Okay — clean thematic statement. Halyard = IP/ownership exploitation. Got it. Houses: AQUALIS, HELION, ASTRA. New proper nouns, but they're introduced visually as insignias, fine.

Page 21: Registry: "INTELLECTUAL ESTATE: ADRIAN PHANTUM / CLAIMANT DETECTED: ALEX PHANTUM / 312 PATENTS — 47 RESTRICTED — 19 DISPUTED." "Three hundred and twelve?" "You said he left you debt." "He left me debt." "Your father left many things badly labeled." Director Cassian Lock approaches, offers signature tablet. "You want the estate." "I'll think about it."

Wait — panel 3 has Alex say "And the people in the records?" and panel 4 has two Alex lines: "You want the estate." / "I'll think about it." Lock never speaks? Lock offers a tablet and Alex just... says "You want the estate. I'll think about it." Lock has zero dialogue on this page. Odd but readable — Lock is silent-polished. Actually as a reader I'd find Lock weirdly mute. He "looks first at the registry, then at Alex" — no line. Hmm.

Also: 312 patents. So Adrian was a massive inventor. And the debt? If dad had 312 patents, why 418,607 credits of debt? The book says the estate is disputed/restricted, but as a reader I immediately ask: why didn't the patents cover the debt? Page 22: "The estate is incomplete because the work was never Adrian's alone." That doesn't answer why the debt stands. Actually maybe the Houses own the patents so the family got nothing? Not explained. Ledger: why does the debt exist alongside a 312-patent estate — never reconciled. Hmm, actually maybe implied: the estate was locked/disputed, so the debt transferred anyway. But it's a question a reader asks.

Page 22: Four collaborators: Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr, Ren Okafor. Five components: membrane purification, living biofilter, distributed nodes, mineral recovery, atmospheric capture. "He left each of them one physical fragment outside the main system." "Lock says a clean owner protects them." "A clean owner also makes them disappear cleanly." "Then we find the dirty version."

Okay — collect-the-five structure. This is a video-game quest structure: gather five fragments from five people. As a reader I now know the shape of issue 2: four fetch quests (Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren — four people, five fragments, Ren has two). Predictable but functional.

Page 23: Lina Vey, Aqualis. "I corrected him. Frequently." "Nearly continuously." Good. The feeder channel contaminated toward Keel. "The Measure exposed routing. It didn't make this feedwater clean." "So the 62 percent comes back through a different pipe." Wait — the 62%? The 62% was "reported to Keel." The contamination is a separate problem. Alex's line "So the 62 percent comes back through a different pipe" — hmm, this conflates the accounting discrepancy with contamination. Lina corrects: "One problem was hidden accounting. This one is physical contamination." Okay so Lina's line clarifies. But Alex's line reads like a non sequitur. Minor confusion.

Membrane fragment handed over. "Find Suri. Tell her I stopped waiting quietly."

Page 24: Suri Anik, biofilter. "The ones who come for Adrian usually want what he built." "Not who he built it with." Living shard. "They removed the team under 'efficiency.' I stayed because something had to keep breathing." "Then don't confuse relief with ownership." These are aphorism-heavy pages. Every collaborator speaks in wise one-liners. Starting to feel like a parade of fortune cookies. As a reader I'm noticing the pattern: each stop = one aphorism + one fragment.

Page 25: Jalen Orr, Helion compute core. "Five people standing still is already a pattern." "They don't watch intentions. They watch repetitions." Node fragment. "No single House or line becomes the throat." "That's why it's dangerous." "That's why I'm not joining you." "Find Ren. If this becomes visible, disappearing won't save us anyway."

Page 26: Ren Okafor, Astra. "Adrian's kid. Took you long enough." "Lina doesn't whisper as quietly as she thinks." Two fragments: mineral recovery, atmospheric capture. "These waste heat. At industrial scale, you vent it." "At household scale?" "You keep it." "Careful gets you buried under a collapse same as reckless." "Adrian didn't build a machine. He built a way for five kinds of work to meet."

Pages 23-26 are four nearly identical scenes: meet collaborator, exchange aphorisms, receive fragment. I skimmed here. It's a montage of wise mentors. The aphorisms blur together. "Careful gets you buried under a collapse same as reckless" — read twice, still not sure what it means in context. Ren says it while a drone passes — meaning caution doesn't protect you, so why be cautious? Okay I guess.

Page 27: Assembly. "Mine fails without the feedwater." "Mine fails without care." "Mine fails if one line owns the route." "Mine fails if waste is treated as waste." "And mine fails if I call it mine." — the parallel structure is very on-the-nose. Central sleeve missing.

Page 28: Prototype sparks, 11% efficiency. "Five standards. Five locks. No shared thread." "Everyone built their piece to protect itself." "What does it need?" "Something that doesn't care who owns the thread." Alex finds a salvaged sleeve. Of course — the Keel scrap kid fixes what the genius Houses couldn't. It's thematically tidy: unregistered scrap as the connective tissue. I see what the book is doing. As a skeptical teen reader, I'd go "of course the orphan's scrap is the answer." But it's satisfying enough.

Page 29: Sleeve filed, KLIK, 91%. "You found the part that wasn't waiting for you." Hmm — read twice. Meaning the other parts were left by his father (waiting for him), but the sleeve is his own contribution. Okay, that's actually a decent line once parsed. But it took a second read.

Page 30: Lock enters with aides. Review notice. Jalen's reassignment, Suri's closure warning, Ren's badge yellow. "Those look identical from here." — meaning the retaliation notices look like the review notice? Read twice. I think Jalen means the punishments and the "review" are the same mechanism. "Quiet isn't the same as safe."

Page 31: Debate. "Sign. We disappear from the record." "Disappearing from the record is what already happened to us once." "If the House takes it, they may scale it." "Or shelve it. Scale is not a promise." "I want out." "Then don't buy your exit with everybody else's name." "Build it small." "Small enough that no House can pretend the people inside it are optional."

Page 32: Build montage. "Same work. Less room to hide it." "Then they take turns." "Put every failure where the user can see it."

Page 33: Toolbox-sized unit. Screen lists requirements: FEEDWATER REQUIRED, MEMBRANE CLEANING REQUIRED, BIOFILTER MAINTENANCE REQUIRED, MINERAL WASTE HANDLING REQUIRED, PATENT STATUS: UNFILED. Cloudy water, useful not miraculous. "Household scale. Maybe block scale." "Not a city." "Without reliable low power, it stops." "Everything stops without something." "Then nobody gets to call it a miracle."

Okay — the book is very insistent on not being a magic fix. I notice the effort. The screen listing maintenance requirements is a nice touch. But the dialogue is getting preachy. "Then nobody gets to call it a miracle" — who would call it a miracle? Nobody did. The book keeps arguing against positions nobody in the scene took. As a reader I feel lectured.

Page 34: Review chamber. "Do you accept administrative transfer of the estate?" "No. The estate isn't mine to transfer." Names the contributors. "Release the design publicly. Leave ownership claims open for human review. Put every name where the House record left a blank."

Page 35: Lina has the Maker's Seal — wait, what? Page 11 showed the Maker's Seal in the workshop as one of the three tools Bi11bot opened. Page 36 panel 3 says "The Seal rests in Alex's hand." But page 35 says "Lina removes the bronze Maker's Seal from inside her uniform. Adrian gave me this before he vanished." So there are... two Seals? Or the Seal from page 11 was given to Lina? No — page 11 the Seal is in the workshop with Bi11bot. Page 35 Lina has it and says Adrian gave it to her. Contradiction? Let me re-read page 11: "Bi11bot opens three compartments: the compact brass Measure, the bronze open-hand Maker's Seal, and three separate dark Covenant bands." So the Seal was in the workshop. Page 35: "Lina removes the bronze Maker's Seal from inside her uniform. 'Adrian gave me this before he vanished. I kept carrying it because nobody had earned the risk.'" That's a flat contradiction — or at least whiplash. As a cold reader: "Wait, didn't the robot already have the Seal? Is this a different one? It says THE Maker's Seal." Confused. This is a genuine continuity stumble a reader would trip on.

Hmm, unless... the page 11 objects were the Measure, the Seal, the bands — and then the Seal was given to Lina at some point off-panel? No, Lina says Adrian gave it to her before he vanished, i.e., fifteen years ago. So the Seal can't have been in the workshop. Contradiction. Finding.

Page 36: Contributors return to Houses, not free but named. Aqualis displays a faster House-controlled version. "They copied it." "They scaled it." "Both can be true." Covenant record: "THIRD NAME WITHHELD." Reflection: a woman with Ada's hair behind the group, not physically present. "One safeguard remains unresolved." "And one name."

Okay — the reflection reveal. Ada's mother, presumably. "THIRD NAME WITHHELD" — the third Covenant custodian. The reflection in black glass is a nice creepy image. But wait — "a woman with Ada's copper-brown hair and steady posture appears behind the group. She is not yet physically present." In a reflection. So... is the reflection showing someone who isn't there? Spooky/impossible? Or is it a video reflection? As a reader: cool image, slightly confusing mechanics. It's a hook though. Ada's mom is the third custodian — I predicted this the moment "THIRD NAME WITHHELD" appeared, given Ada's mysterious backstory (the rivet-touching, "my mother" hints... actually were there hints? Page 3: "She touches one rivet on her shoulder strap." Page 38: same rivet. The rivet is a tell. But no explicit mother mention until page 38. Actually the withheld name + reflection = obviously mom).

Issue 2 verdict: the collect-the-fragments structure is clear but repetitive; pages 23-26 blur. The Seal contradiction confused me. The ending hook (Ada's mom) works. Last page: I'd continue, mild yes.

**Issue 03 — Oasis**

Page 37: Oasis. "TEMPORARY ACCESS — ESCORT REQUIRED." Ada's gate opens immediately: "VEYRA, A. — RESIDENT RECORD FOUND — STATUS: UNRESOLVED." "It knew my name." Good hook payoff. So Ada has an Oasis record. Confirms the mom thing.

Page 38: Covenant custodians: ADRIAN PHANTUM, MERA VALE, LEONA VEYRA. "Leona." "My mother." "You thought she was gone." "I thought she had disappeared. I stopped asking whether that meant dead or unwilling." "Now I know which question to ask." Okay — so Mera Vale is a custodian. The Mera from page 12 who chose TRACK and (apparently) authorized the flood. Now she's a custodian of the Covenant. And the flood thing is STILL not addressed. Hmm.

Wait, also — Ada's mom is a Covenant custodian, and Ada never knew? Ada's been in Keel for years. Her mom disappeared. And Ada never mentioned any of this to Alex? The book treats Ada's backstory as a sealed box until now. As a reader I feel like the book withheld rather than the character. Also — did Bi11bot know? Bi11bot knew the custodians presumably. The "THIRD NAME WITHHELD" on page 36 — withheld from whom? Bi11bot's own record? If Bi11bot knew Leona, why withheld? Eh.

Page 39: Leona's door. "I knew this day would come." "I didn't." "Would you like something?" "I didn't come for tea." — callback to Ada's "Tea’s free" on page 3. Nice echo, I caught it.

Page 40: "Did you know where I was?" "Within a year." "Alpha could have told me exactly where. I chose not to go." "I believed knowing me would make you a target." "You chose safety for me." "Yes." "You chose it instead of me." "I thought I was trading a few terrible days I could see for years I couldn't." "You traded my choice."

Okay — this scene is the emotional core of issue 3 and it mostly works. "You chose it instead of me" lands. But it's also very... tidy. Everyone speaks in perfectly balanced thesis statements. Real estranged mother-daughter reunions are messier. As a teen reader, I might roll eyes at how articulate everyone is about their own trauma. But the content is strong.

Page 41: Mera enters. "Alpha tracked everyone connected to Adrian." "I suppressed your association risk from the active reports. I could not erase the network's inferences." "You hid me and watched me." "Yes." "That isn't protection." "No. It was the part of the protection I could still perform." "My silence for your protection." "And your silence kept Alpha's authority unchallenged."

Okay, Mera protected Ada. So Mera was good all along? THEN WHO FLOODED THE CONDUIT? Page 18 said "Mera's authorization reaches a conduit valve. CONDUIT SEGMENT — RELEASE AUTHORIZED." If Mera is protective, the flood makes no sense. Unless Alpha did it using her credentials? Never explained. This bugs me a lot. It's the biggest dangling thread.

Page 42: The box. Leona's band, childhood photos, toy. "There were three of us. Adrian, Mera, and me." Water-Wars aftermath memory: seized infrastructure, guarded stores, families separated, flooded streets. "The Covenant failed when fear made promises smaller than survival." "Alpha could take emergency authority if two of us agreed. Adrian said no. Mera said yes." "And you?" "I made the deciding choice." "I chose what I could control. Then the temporary answer became fifteen years."

FINALLY — the water wars and the Covenant explained, on page 42 of 54. The reader.md says readers don't know what the water wars or safeguards are until the book tells them — the book tells them very late and very briefly. "Water-Wars aftermath" gets one memory panel.
